transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Gritty bits are usually food being recirculated or detergent/salt not dissolving properly. Try these, roughly in order of likelihood:

1. Clean the filter (most common cause)
• Pull out the bottom basket. The filter is in the base, usually under the lower spray arm.
• Twist anticlockwise and lift out. It's normally 2-3 parts (a cylinder, a fine mesh, and a coarse plate).
• Rinse under a hot tap and scrub with an old toothbrush. Get any gunk out of the sump hole underneath.
• On Beko models this should be done every couple of weeks, and it's often never been done.

2. Check the spray arms
• Spin them by hand. They should turn freely.
• Look for blocked holes (seeds, bits of glass, limescale). Poke them clear with a cocktail stick.
• The arms usually unclip or unscrew, so you can rinse them through.
• Don't forget the top arm under the upper basket.

3. Check the salt cap
• If the salt cap is loose or cross-threaded, salt can leak into the wash and leave a gritty or white residue.
• Make sure it's screwed on tight, and wipe up any spilled salt after refilling.

4. Detergent
• If tablets aren't dissolving fully, they can leave grainy bits. Check whether there's a lump left in the drawer after a cycle.
• Try a different brand, and make sure nothing tall (like a board or tray) blocks the dispenser flap from opening.
• Powder can clump if it's old or damp.

5. Program choice
• Eco and quick washes run cooler and shorter, and often don't clear food properly.
• Try a hotter cycle (e.g. 65°C Intensive) to see if it improves.

6. Loading
• Scrape plates well (no need to rinse, but get big bits off).
• Don't overcrowd. Bowls should face down and inwards towards the spray.
• Make sure nothing hangs down and stops the arms spinning.

7. Run a cleaning cycle
• Once the filter is clean, run an empty hot wash with dishwasher cleaner (Finish, Dr Beckmann etc.) or a cup of white vinegar upright in the top rack.

8. Check it's draining
• If there's standing water in the bottom after a cycle, the drain hose may be kinked or the sink waste/trap blocked, which sends dirty water back over the dishes.

If you've done all that and it's still gritty, the wash pump or a spray arm could be faulty. That's worth a Beko engineer visit, especially if it's still under warranty.

Start with the filter. I'd bet that's it 👍 Let me know what you find.
ok will try the filter first. its a quick 30 min wash i usually use if that matters

Yes, that matters a lot, and it's probably part of the problem.

Why the 30 min quick wash struggles:
• It runs cooler (often around 35-40°C) and much shorter, so tablets often don't fully dissolve, which leaves exactly the gritty residue you're describing.
• It has less time to break down food, so bits get recirculated and redeposited on glasses and bowls.
• It's really meant for lightly soiled, freshly used dishes, not a full load of dinner plates.

What to do:
• Clean the filter first as planned. A clogged filter plus a short wash is a bad combo.
• Switch to Eco or Auto for normal loads. Eco takes longer (often 3+ hours) but cleans better and actually uses less energy, because it soaks at lower heat for longer.
• Use Intensive (65-70°C) for greasy or heavily dirty loads.
• If you stick with quick wash, use powder or gel instead of tablets (they dissolve faster), and keep loads light and well scraped.

Finishing off the last tip I got cut off on:
After a cycle, check for standing water in the bottom. If there's more than a small puddle, it's not draining properly. That's usually from a blocked filter or a kinked or blocked drain hose, which would also cause dirty water to sit and redeposit grit.

Try the filter plus one Eco or Intensive cycle, and you'll likely see a big difference straight away.

ok did the filter, it was full of food n grease lol. also upper spray arm was stiff n some holes blocked with seeds/limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick. ran a normal programme after n its much better

Great result! A filter full of food and grease plus blocked spray arm holes would definitely explain the gritty glasses and bowls.

To keep it working well:
• Clean the filter every 2-4 weeks. It only takes a couple of minutes once you know how.
• Check the spray arms every month or two, especially the top one, and give them a quick spin to make sure they turn freely.
• Run an empty hot cleaning cycle monthly with dishwasher cleaner to clear grease and limescale.
• Use Eco or a normal programme as your default, and save the quick wash for light, freshly used loads.

The limescale suggests hard water, so:
• Keep the salt topped up. It softens the water and stops scale building up in the arms and on glasses.
• Use rinse aid to help prevent cloudy glasses and spots.
• Check the water hardness setting. Beko machines have one, and it's often left on the factory default. Your local water supplier's website will tell you your hardness level, and the manual explains how to set it.
